react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on a single biological axis: disruption of arachidonic acid metabolism and eicosanoid biosynthesis. RaMP multi-database ORA identifies Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top hit with FDR 2.1×10⁻¹³, driven by five input metabolites — arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219), leukotriene A4 (KEGG:C00909), 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-prostaglandin J2 (KEGG:C14717), 5(S)-HETE (KEGG:C04805), and 15(S)-HETE (KEGG:C04742) — against a pathway roster of 27 compounds, yielding a raw hypergeometric p-value of 1.18×10⁻¹⁵ and fold-enrichment of 1,251. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently recovers the same biological module as its top-ranked KEGG entry hsa00590 (arachidonic acid metabolism), with four of the same driver metabolites (arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 5-HETE, 15-HETE). Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis corroborates this as its highest-significance hit (p=0.0059, overlap=11/11 compounds in the MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism module) and additionally flags prostaglandin formation from arachidonate (rank 3, p=0.041) and leukotriene metabolism (rank 4, p=0.041), confirming that both the lipoxygenase and cyclooxygenase arms of the eicosanoid cascade are transcriptionally or post-translationally perturbed. The convergent signal across ORA (RaMP), KEGG-namespace PSEA, and empirical m/z networking identifies arachidonic acid as the upstream substrate and 5(S)-HETE / 15(S)-HETE as the primary oxidized lipid effectors, with leukotriene A4 and 15-deoxy-PGJ2 representing the downstream cysteinyl-leukotriene and cyclopentenone prostaglandin branches. Two input metabolites — methylmalonic acid (associated with propionyl-CoA accumulation and mitochondrial dysfunction) and xanthine (purine catabolism) — do not map to the eicosanoid module, suggesting that a separate metabolic stress axis is also present but not enriched in the lipid-centric paradigm. The consistent 4-to-5 compound hit overlap across all three methods, with FDR well below 10⁻¹² in ORA, constitutes robust multi-paradigm evidence that the treatment condition drives a coordinated perturbation of the arachidonic acid-eicosanoid signaling network, with likely implications for inflammation, oxidative stress, and lipid-mediated cell signaling.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on the Eicosanoid synthesis module (WP:WP167) as the dominant biological signal. RaMP multi-database ORA identifies Eicosanoid synthesis as the top-ranked hit with FDR 2.12e-13, raw hypergeometric p-value 1.18e-15, fold enrichment 1250.95, and 5 of 27 pathway members detected (arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-deoxy-delta-12,14-PGJ2, 5-HETE, 15-HETE). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently recovers the same biological module at its top-ranked KEGG entry (hsa00590), with 4 of 44 metabolites in the input set mapping to this pathway (arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 5-HETE, 15-HETE). Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis corroborates this finding as its highest-significance hit (p-value 0.0043), with an 11-of-11 compound overlap in the MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism module. Arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219) is the upstream substrate common to both the cyclooxygenase and lipoxygenase arms of the pathway; it is directly converted by PTGS1 (COX-1) and PTGS2 (COX-2) to downstream eicosanoids including 5-HETE (KEGG:C04805) via the 5-lipoxygenase branch and 15-HETE (KEGG:C04742) via the 15-lipoxygenase branch. Leukotriene A4 (KEGG:C00909) occupies the cysteinyl-leukotriene branch, and 15-deoxy-delta-12,14-PGJ2 (KEGG:C14717) occupies the cyclopentenone prostaglandin branch. Three input metabolites (methylmalonic acid, thiosulfate, and xanthine) do not map to the eicosanoid synthesis module, indicating a separate metabolic stress axis distinct from the lipid-centered signal.

RaMP multi-database ORA identifies Eicosanoid synthesis as the top-ranked hit with FDR 2.12e-13, raw hypergeometric p-value 1.18e-15, fold enrichment 1250.95, and 5 of 27 pathway members detected (arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-deoxy-delta-12,14-PGJ2, 5-HETE, 15-HETE). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently recovers the same biological module at its top-ranked KEGG entry (hsa00590), with 4 of 44 metabolites in the input set mapping to this pathway (arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 5-HETE, 15-HETE). Arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219) is the upstream substrate common to both the cyclooxygenase and lipoxygenase arms of the pathway; it is directly converted by PTGS1 (COX-1) and PTGS2 (COX-2) to downstream eicosanoids including 5-HETE (KEGG:C04805) via the 5-lipoxygenase branch and 15-HETE (KEGG:C04742) via the 15-lipoxygenase branch. RaMP multi-database ORA identifies Eicosanoid synthesis as the top-ranked hit with FDR 2.12e-13, raw hypergeometric p-value 1.18e-15, fold enrichment 1250.95, and 5 of 27 pathway members detected (arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-deoxy-delta-12,14-PGJ2, 5-HETE, 15-HETE). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently recovers the same biological module at its top-ranked KEGG entry (hsa00590), with 4 of 44 metabolites in the input set mapping to this pathway (arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 5-HETE, 15-HETE). Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis corroborates this finding as its highest-significance hit (p-value 0.0043), with an 11-of-11 compound overlap in the MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism module. Arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219) is the upstream substrate common to both the cyclooxygenase and lipoxygenase arms of the pathway; it is directly converted by PTGS1 (COX-1) and PTGS2 (COX-2) to downstream eicosanoids including 5-HETE (KEGG:C04805) via the 5-lipoxygenase branch and 15-HETE (KEGG:C04742) via the 15-lipoxygenase branch. Leukotriene A4 (KEGG:C00909) occupies the cysteinyl-leukotriene branch, and 15-deoxy-delta-12,14-PGJ2 (KEGG:C14717) occupies the cyclopentenone prostaglandin branch. Three input metabolites (methylmalonic acid, thiosulfate, and xanthine) do not map to the eicosanoid synthesis module, indicating a separate metabolic stress axis distinct from the lipid-centered signal.
